name: JC Glancy
current_role: Co-founder, ZenBusiness; Venture Partner, Fluent Ventures
profile: JC (James) Glancy co-founded ZenBusiness, the Austin-based all-in-one platform that helps small businesses form, run and grow (LLC formation, compliance, banking, accounting), valued around $1.7B in 2021. He brought in HomeAway founding CTO Ross Buhrdorf as investor and later CEO. He is now a venture partner at Fluent Ventures and an angel/advisor.
interesting_fact: ZenBusiness took roughly a 10-year journey to become an 'overnight success'; Glancy says his drive came from wanting to make life easier for small-business owners like his father.
deep_cut_fact: Glancy deliberately hired his own boss, bringing in Ross Buhrdorf as CEO, summing up the trade-off as: "You can either be rich or be king." He also noted ZenBusiness customers who use its banking churn at half the rate of those who don't.
notes: Low public profile; Ross Buhrdorf is ZenBusiness's public face. Fluent Ventures (Alex Lazarow) is a warm route - Glancy is a venture partner there.

name: Nicolas Bacca
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, ZKNox (hardware security & zero-knowledge cryptography); angel investor
profile: French hardware-security engineer who co-founded Ledger (2014), the Paris crypto hardware-wallet unicorn, serving as CTO and from 2019 chief innovation officer until leaving in 2023. After briefly launching smart-wallet project Smoo.th, he co-founded ZKNox in 2025 with cryptographers from Ledger and Thales, and angel-invests in French crypto startups (Bitstack, Spiko, Bubblemaps, Hyli).
interesting_fact: He read the Bitcoin whitepaper in 2012 while holding a smart-card design that could store secrets but had no business model: 'Bitcoin gave me that. So I'm very grateful for Satoshi.'
deep_cut_fact: As a child he printed his own fake banknotes and 'paid' his parents with them ('I was kind of my own central bank'); today he's invested in a champagne house that pays dividends in bottles, and says he's famous for bringing champagne to every party.
notes: Long known in crypto by the handle 'btchip' (on Devcon profile) - personal X not independently verified here. Speaks regularly at Paris Blockchain Week, EthCC, Devcon; conference circuit is a natural route. Ledger's Recover controversy preceded his exit - avoid.

name: Eli Broverman
current_role: Co-founder, Treasury (early-stage fintech venture fund); co-founder of Betterment
profile: Securities lawyer who co-founded robo-advisor Betterment with Jon Stein in 2008, serving as President/COO and building its legal/regulatory structure, broker-dealer and 401(k) business. He stepped back from day-to-day operations in 2017 (staying on the board/advisory) and co-founded Treasury, an early-stage fintech fund with Acorns founders, which led Betterment's 2021 $60M Series F.
interesting_fact: Betterment's founders needed a lawyer willing to take risk: Stein realised automated advice needed a regulatory structure built from scratch, and Broverman, a lawyer who 'had been wanting to start something', built it at Stein's kitchen table.
deep_cut_fact: He first met Betterment co-founder Jon Stein at a poker table around 2003 - 'Little did I know that we would soon be working together at his kitchen table building a company...' He calls himself a masochist who loves a company's 'formative period'.
notes: Low public profile; no longer operational at Betterment so company press is an indirect route. Treasury fund (with Jeff Cruttenden/Acorns) is a better angle; Milken Institute speaker profile exists.

name: Hadas Amitay
current_role: Listed co-founder of Orca Security (current role not publicly documented)
profile: Hadas Amitay appears (sometimes as 'Amitay Hadas') in founder lists of Orca Security, the Tel Aviv-founded agentless cloud-security (CNAPP) company started in 2019 by eight colleagues largely from Check Point, which reached a $1.8B valuation in 2021. No public biography, title or current role was found.
interesting_fact: Orca was founded by eight co-founders - unusually large for a startup - most of them former Check Point colleagues, and pioneered 'SideScanning', agentless cloud-workload scanning.
notes: Very low public footprint; only insider-data aggregators (MarketScreener) list the name. Name order/spelling inconsistent. Public faces of Orca are CEO Avi Shua and Gil Geron - route via them/company press.

name: Forest Lee
current_role: Co-founder, Sendbird (formerly Head of Design; aggregator profiles list an 'AI Agent Workforce Manager' role since 2025)
profile: Forest Lee is one of the four co-founders of Sendbird (2013, Korea; now San Mateo), the chat/messaging API company valued at $1.05B in 2021 that has pivoted to AI customer-service agents (Delight.ai). He led Sendbird's product design for over a decade; CEO John S. Kim is the company's public face.
interesting_fact: Sendbird began in Seoul in 2013 as a community app for mothers; the team pulled out its messaging engine and turned it into a B2B chat API, becoming only the second Korean company backed by Y Combinator (W16).
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Current role per aggregator profiles (Crunchbase/Humantic) only - verify on LinkedIn. Founder rosters vary by source; MarketScreener lists him as co-founder. Origin story detail also at https://koreatechdesk.com/?p=1370. Route via CEO John Kim/company.

name: Josh Williams
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Forte (blockchain gaming infrastructure) - current status as of 2026 not re-verified
profile: Serial games/tech entrepreneur who co-founded Forte (~2018) with Kabam founder Kevin Chou to give game developers compliant blockchain infrastructure (ownership of in-game goods, token/economy design). Forte raised $725M in 2021 at a ~$1B valuation, backed by a $100M developer fund. He previously led indie game-engine company GarageGames as CEO/CTO.
interesting_fact: Forte's $100M developer fund gave grants to game studios to integrate blockchain without asking for equity or revenue share; early partners included Kongregate, Netmarble and Hi-Rez Studios.
deep_cut_fact: Before Forte, Williams spent ~20 years in machine learning, real-time tech and big data, and was CEO/CTO of GarageGames, the indie engine company (Torque) that was an early pioneer of digitally distributed games.
notes: Common name - make sure outreach targets Forte's Josh Williams (San Francisco), not Gowalla's or Very Great's. Forte site (forte.io) blocked automated fetch; no published press email found. Long-form interview: Naavik podcast https://naavik.co/podcast/forte/. Web-search budget ran out mid-lane; 2026 status unverified.

name: Phil DeGisi
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product & Marketing Officer, Orchard (as of 2022; current title not re-verified)
profile: Phil DeGisi co-founded Orchard, the 'buy before you sell' real-estate tech company that lets homeowners purchase a new home before selling their old one, which reached a $1B+ valuation within about four years. He leads Orchard's product and marketing teams, growing marketing from one person to a 30-person department.
interesting_fact: Named a HousingWire 2022 Marketing Leader; in Orchard's early days he personally met with hundreds of homeowners to understand the pain of buying and selling a home.
notes: Low public profile. Web-search budget exhausted mid-lane, so background/deep-cut research was limited to direct page fetches.

name: Ryan Wong
profile: Vancouver-based business-intelligence veteran who co-founded Visier (2010), the people-analytics / 'Workforce AI' software company valued at $1B+. Before Visier he spent 20+ years in BI at Crystal Decisions, Business Objects and SAP, ending as VP Engineering for SAP BusinessObjects. Visier now pitches AI talent agents built on enterprise workforce data.
interesting_fact: Visier's leadership grew out of the Crystal Reports lineage: Wong rode Crystal Decisions through its acquisition by Business Objects and then SAP, before co-founding Visier to apply analytics to HR/workforce data.
deep_cut_fact: Wong was the original author and Chief Software Architect of the Crystal Enterprise platform, the server product behind Crystal Reports' enterprise reporting business.
notes: Technical founder; data/AI angle fits the podcast. Common name - target Visier's Ryan Wong (Vancouver).

name: Anthony Welters
current_role: Executive Chairman, BlackIvy Group; Co-Founder & Chairman, Somatus
profile: Harlem-raised lawyer turned healthcare entrepreneur (b. 1955) who founded Medicaid managed-care firm AmeriChoice in 1989, sold it to UnitedHealth Group and rose to EVP/Office of the CEO there. He co-founded and chairs Somatus, a value-based kidney-care company valued at $2.5B, and since 2014 chairs BlackIvy, which builds food, housing, healthcare and logistics businesses in Sub-Saharan Africa.
interesting_fact: Before AmeriChoice he started several businesses, from manufacturing to restaurant franchises, which all failed: 'You have to be prepared to accept failure to have success.' His break came in 1988 when he won Philadelphia's Medicaid-management contract, then Pennsylvania's largest ever.
deep_cut_fact: As a boy he shined shoes under the elevated subway and swept a barbershop floor for tips; he skipped fourth grade, got into Stuyvesant, finished Manhattanville College in under three years, and earned his NYU law degree at 22. He and his wife Bea founded Camp Dogwood Summer Academy for low-income kids in Virginia's Blue Ridge.
notes: Horatio Alger Award 1998; NYU Law lobby named for him; vice chair NYU trustees; AnBryce Scholarship founder. Avoid the Clarence Thomas RV-loan story (on Wikipedia). Somatus site blocks automated access; no press email captured.

name: Christopher Kemper
current_role: Founder, Chairman (and CEO per media page), Palmetto Clean Technology
profile: Chris Kemper founded Palmetto (2010, Charleston SC), a home clean-energy platform selling and financing residential solar, batteries, HVAC/heat pumps and its 'LightReach' energy plans through local installer partners; it reached a $1B+ valuation. He frames Palmetto as a 'New Utility' building a decentralized, decarbonized energy future.
interesting_fact: Palmetto hired former FERC chairman Neil Chatterjee as Chief Governmental Affairs Officer - he writes on issues like FERC large-load (data-center) interconnection - and ex-NBA player Shane Battier as Chief Culture Advisor; Jigar Shah and Chamath Palihapitiya are listed advisors.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast (residential solar + grid/large-load policy via Chatterjee). Leadership page lists Kemper as Chairman/Director; media page still says Founder, Chairman and CEO - confirm current CEO title. Web-search budget exhausted, so no sourced personal deep cut.

name: David Briggs
current_role: Listed co-founder of GeoComply (current title not confirmed on company site)
profile: David Briggs is listed as a co-founder of GeoComply, the Vancouver-based geolocation-compliance and fraud-prevention company founded in 2011 whose technology verifies users' locations for regulated online gaming, streaming and fintech; it reached a $1B+ valuation. Co-founder Anna Sainsbury chairs the company and is its public face; no public bio for Briggs was found.
interesting_fact: GeoComply's location checks underpin legal US online sports betting - operators must prove each bettor is physically inside a permitting state, a market GeoComply's tech helped make possible.
notes: Very common name - confirm it is GeoComply's co-founder. GeoComply site blocks automated fetch and does not name him; web-search budget exhausted before a bio could be found. Interesting fact is a general industry characterization; source page only confirms 2011 founding/mission.
